title.zh: 第十九 郡國一 司隷
title.en: Volume 109: Commanderies and States Part One
title.raw: 第十九 郡國一 司隷 Volume 109: Commanderies and States Part One

translations.literal: Treatise Nineteen: Commanderies and States, Part One
translations.idiomatic: Treatise 19: Commanderies and Principalities, Part I

sentences.zh: 《汉书·地理志》记天下郡县本末及山川奇异、风俗所由，至矣。

translations.literal: The 'Treatise on Geography' in the Hanshu records the origins and outcomes of commanderies and counties throughout the realm, together with strange mountains and rivers and the sources of local customs; it is exhaustive.
translations.idiomatic: The Geography Treatise in the Book of Han exhaustively traces every commandery and county in the empire, notes remarkable mountains and rivers, and explains how regional customs arose.

sentences.zh: 今但录中兴以来郡县改异及《春秋》、三史会同征伐地名，以为《郡国志》。

translations.literal: Here we record only, since the restoration, changes in commanderies and counties, as well as place names attested in the Spring and Autumn Annals and in the Three Histories when they jointly confirm campaigns of conquest, to form this 'Treatise on Commanderies and States.'
translations.idiomatic: This chapter records only post-restoration changes among commanderies and counties, plus battle-related placenames where the Spring and Autumn and the three standard histories agree—hence the title Commanderies and States.

sentences.zh: 凡《前志》有县名今所不载者，皆世祖所并省也。

translations.literal: Whenever a county name appeared in the previous treatise but is not carried here, it was merged or abolished by Emperor Guangwu.
translations.idiomatic: Any county listed in the earlier Geography but omitted here was folded into another unit or struck from the rolls under Emperor Guangwu.

translations.literal: Those not existing before but existing now were established in later times.
translations.idiomatic: Entries that had no Western Han predecessor were added in subsequent reigns.

sentences.zh: 凡县名先书者，郡所治也。

translations.literal: Whenever a county name is written first, it is the seat of the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The county named first in each list is the commandery seat.

sentences.zh: 河南 河内 河东 弘农 京兆 冯翊 扶风

translations.literal: Henan, Henei, Hedong, Hongnong, Jingzhao, Fengyi, Fufeng.
translations.idiomatic: The Inspectorate lists the commanderies Henan, Henei, Hedong, Hongnong, Jingzhao, Fengyi, and Fufeng.

sentences.zh: ◎ 河南尹秦三川郡，高帝更名。

translations.literal: ◎ The Administrator of Henan — under Qin it was the Three Rivers Commandery; Emperor Gaozu renamed it.
translations.idiomatic: ◎ Henan (Administrator's jurisdiction): Qin's Three Rivers Commandery, renamed under Emperor Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 世祖都雒阳，建武十五年改曰河南尹。

translations.literal: When Emperor Guangwu took Luoyang as his capital, in the fifteenth year of Jianwu it was renamed Administrator of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: After Guangwu fixed his capital at Luoyang, Jianwu 15 elevated the office to Administrator of Henan.

sentences.zh: 二十一城，永和五年户二十万八千四百八十六，口百一万八百二十七。

translations.literal: Twenty-one cities; in the fifth year of Yonghe, households 208,486, mouths 1,012,027.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-one county seats; the Yonghe 5 census recorded 208,486 households and 1,012,027 people.

translations.literal: 〖Luoyang〗 In Zhou times it was called Chengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: 〖Luoyang〗 Zhou documents knew it as Chengzhou.

translations.literal: There is Di Spring; it is inside the city.
translations.idiomatic: Di Spring lies within the city.
It includes the settlement of Tang.
It includes the settlement of Shangcheng.
It includes the settlement of Shixiang.
It includes the Chu surname settlement.

sentences.zh: 〖河南〗周公时所城雒邑也，春秋时谓之王城。

translations.literal: 〖Henan〗 It is the walled Luoyi built by the dukes of Zhou; in Spring and Autumn times it was called the royal city.
translations.idiomatic: 〖Henan County〗 This is the Luoyi fortified by the Western Zhou dukes; Spring and Autumn sources call it the royal capital.

sentences.zh: 东城门名鼎门，北城门名乾祭。

translations.literal: The east gate is named Ding Gate; the north gate is named Ganji.
translations.idiomatic: Its east gate was Ding Gate; its north gate, Ganji.

translations.literal: There is also Gan city; there is Kuai township.
translations.idiomatic: It also holds Gan city and Kuai township.

translations.literal: 〖Liang〗 A former state; descendants of Boyi.
translations.idiomatic: 〖Liang〗 Ancient polity, traditionally the line of Boyi.
Huoyang Mountain lies within its borders.

translations.literal: There is Guo pavilion; the state of Guo Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Guo pavilion marks the domain associated with Guo Shu.

translations.literal: 〖Juan〗 There is the Long Wall; it passes Yangwu to Mi.
translations.idiomatic: 〖Juan〗 The Long Wall runs through here, from Yangwu toward Mi.

translations.literal: There is Yuanyong city; some say it is ancient Hengyong.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyong city—identified by some as ancient Hengyong—stands here.
The mouth of the Qingshui River is here.
〖Wanling〗 The text records a forest whose name is lost to lacunae.
〖Gucheng〗 A river whose name is partly unreadable in the manuscript rises here.
〖Goushi〗 Wu settlement lies within the county.
〖Gong〗 The Xungu River flows through the county.

translations.literal: There is Dongzi settlement; today called Zi city.
translations.idiomatic: Dongzi settlement—now known as Zi city—is recorded here.
There is a Kan-settlement whose second character is missing in the received text.
Mei Mountain lies within the county.
Xing Mountain lies within the county.

translations.literal: There is □ settlement; ancient □ clan; today named Manzhong.
translations.idiomatic: A settlement whose ancient surname is missing in the text is today called Manzhong.

translations.literal: 〖Yanshi〗 There is Shi township; in Spring and Autumn times called Shi clan.
translations.idiomatic: 〖Yanshi〗 Shi township—the Spring and Autumn Annals call it the Shi lineage.

translations.literal: 〖Xinzheng〗 The Classic of Poetry's Zheng state; the mound of Zhurong.
translations.idiomatic: 〖Xinzheng〗 Zheng of the Odes; the ruined mound of Zhurong.

translations.literal: ◎ Henei Commandery — established by Emperor Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: ◎ Henei Commandery, founded under Emperor Gaozu.

translations.literal: One hundred twenty li north of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: It lies one hundred twenty li north of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 十八城，户十五万九千七百七十，口八十万一千五百五十八。

translations.idiomatic: Eighteen counties; the registers show 159,770 households and 801,558 people.
〖Huai〗 The county contains a city whose name is damaged in the manuscript.
〖Zhi〗 Yuan township lies within the county.
The place called □ Liang—second character unreadable—is recorded here.
〖Bo〗 A walled town whose name is incomplete in the text.
Another city name survives only as a lacuna in the sources.

translations.literal: 〖Wen〗 Where the Su lords established their seat.
translations.idiomatic: 〖Wen〗 Ancient seat of the Su lineage.

sentences.zh: 济水出，王莽时大旱，遂枯绝。

translations.literal: The Ji River rises; under Wang Mang there was great drought, and it dried up entirely.
translations.idiomatic: The Ji River rises here; Wang Mang's drought years left its channel dry.

sentences.zh: 〖平睾〗有邢丘，故邢国，周公子所封。

translations.literal: 〖Pinggao〗 There is Xingqiu; the former Xing state; where the Duke of Zhou's son was enfeoffed.
translations.idiomatic: 〖Pinggao〗 Xingqiu preserves the old Xing polity enfeoffed to a son of the Duke of Zhou.
Li city lies within the county.

translations.literal: 〖Xiuwu〗 Formerly Nanyang; Emperor Qin Shi Huang renamed it.
translations.idiomatic: 〖Xiuwu〗 Once called Nanyang until Qin Shi Huang rechristened it.

translations.literal: There is Nanyang city; Yangfan; Zanmao fields.
translations.idiomatic: Sites include Nanyang city, Yangfan, and the Zanmao fields.
Little Xiuwu settlement is recorded here.
〖Gong〗 Territory of the ancient Gong polity.
The Qi River has its source here.
The county lists a pavilion whose name is lost to lacunae.

sentences.zh: 〖朝歌〗纣所都居，南有牧野，北有邶国，南有宁乡。

translations.literal: 〖Zhaoge〗 Where King Zhou made his seat; to the south is Muye; to the north is the Bei state; to the south is Ning township.
translations.idiomatic: 〖Zhaoge〗 King Zhou's capital: Muye lies south, the Bei polity north, and Ning township farther south.
〖Dangyin〗 A walled town recorded as □ Li—the first character is missing.

translations.literal: 〖Linlu〗 Formerly Longlu; Emperor Shang renamed it.
translations.idiomatic: 〖Linlu〗 Once Longlu until Emperor Shang rechristened it.

sentences.zh: ◎ 河东郡秦置，雒阳西北五百里。

translations.literal: ◎ Hedong Commandery — established under Qin; five hundred li northwest of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: ◎ Hedong Commandery: a Qin foundation lying five hundred li northwest of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 二十城，户九万三千五百四十三，口五十七万八百三。

translations.idiomatic: Twenty counties; registers record 93,543 households and 570,803 people.

translations.literal: 〖Anyi〗 There is iron; there is a salt pond.
translations.idiomatic: 〖Anyi〗 Known for ironworks and its salt lagoon.
〖Yang〗 Gaoliang pavilion stands within the county.
Tradition places Emperor Yao's capital here.
〖Fenyin〗 Jie Mountain rises in the county.

translations.literal: 〖Dayang〗 There is Wu Mountain; on its heights is Yu city.
translations.idiomatic: 〖Dayang〗 Wu Mountain carries the ruins of Yu city on its summit.
Xiayang city lies within the county.
The Dianling escarpment runs through the county.
〖Pishi〗 Geng township lies within the borders.
〖Wenxi〗 Administered as a town; ancient seat of Quwo.

translations.literal: There is Dong Pool marsh; the ancient Dong marsh.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Pool preserves the old Dong marsh.

translations.literal: 〖Yong'an〗 Formerly □; renamed in the second year of Yangjia.
translations.idiomatic: 〖Yong'an〗 Earlier name lost in lacunae; rechristened under Emperor Shun's Yangjia 2.

translations.literal: 〖Hebei〗 The Wei state of the 《Classic of Poetry》.
translations.idiomatic: 〖Hebei〗 The Wei polity celebrated in the 《Classic of Poetry》.

translations.literal: 〖Yuan〗 There is Wangwu Mountain; Yan water rises.
translations.idiomatic: 〖Yuan〗 Wangwu Mountain; the Yan River has its source here.
Huqiu pavilion lies within the county.
Shao pavilion lies within the county.

translations.literal: ◎ Hongnong Commandery — established by Emperor Wu.
translations.idiomatic: ◎ Hongnong Commandery, founded under Emperor Wu.

translations.literal: Its two counties were attached in the fifteenth year of Jianwu.
translations.idiomatic: Two of its counties were transferred in under Jianwu 15.

translations.literal: Four hundred fifty li southwest of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: It lies four hundred fifty li southwest of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 九城，户四万六千八百一十五，口十九万九千一百一十三。

translations.literal: 〖Hongnong〗 The old Qin Hangu Pass; Zhu water rises.
translations.idiomatic: 〖Hongnong〗 Site of Qin's Hangu Pass; the Zhu River rises here.
Kucong Mountain lies within the county.

translations.literal: There is Taoqiu settlement; the ancient Peach Grove.
translations.idiomatic: Taoqiu preserves the ground of the Peach Grove.

translations.literal: 〖Shan〗 Originally the state of Guo Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: 〖Shan〗 Territory of Eastern Guo's Guo Zhong line.
The Shan mo divide is here.
The Two Xiaos defiles lie here.

translations.literal: 〖Luhun〗 To the west lies territory taken from Guo.
〖Lushi〗 There is Xiong'er Gate; Yi water and Qingshui rise.
translations.idiomatic: 〖Lushi〗 At Xiong'er Gate the Yi and Qingshui rivers begin.
Mount Taihua—the great Hua peak—dominates the county.

translations.literal: ◎ Administrator of Jingzhao — Qin Inner Historian; Emperor Wu renamed it.
translations.idiomatic: ◎ Jingzhao (capital intendancy): Qin's Inner Historian circuit, rechristened under Emperor Wu.

translations.literal: Its four counties were attached in the fifteenth year of Jianwu.
translations.idiomatic: Four counties joined the intendancy in Jianwu 15.

translations.literal: Nine hundred fifty li west of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Nine hundred fifty li west of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 十城，户五万三千二百九十九，口二十八万五千五百七十四。

translations.idiomatic: 〖Chang'an〗 Western Han capital founded by Emperor Gaozu.
The site of Hao lies inside the imperial Shanglin Park.

translations.literal: There is Quyou; there is Duyou.

translations.idiomatic: 〖Duling〗 Feng township sits southwest of the seat.

sentences.zh: 〖新丰〗有骊山，东有鸿门亭及戏亭。

translations.literal: 〖Xinfeng〗 There is Li Mountain; to the east are Hongmen pavilion and Xi pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: 〖Xinfeng〗 Li Mountain; eastward lie Hongmen and Xi pavilions.
A walled settlement whose name is incomplete in the received text.

translations.literal: There is Zhongling Mountain; Luo water rises.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongling Mountain; the Luo River rises here.
It used to fall under Hongnong.
Tuhe Mountain lies within the county.

sentences.zh: ◎ 左冯翊秦属内史，武帝分，改名。

translations.literal: ◎ Governor of Zuo Fengyi — under Qin it belonged to the Inner Historian; Emperor Wu split it off and changed the name.
translations.idiomatic: ◎ Zuo Fengyi: carved from Qin's Inner Historian territory under Emperor Wu.

translations.literal: Six hundred eighty-eight li west of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Six hundred eighty-eight li west of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 十三城，户三万七千九十，口十四万五千一百九十五。

translations.literal: 〖Duyu〗 Summer of the ninth year of Yongyuan.
translations.idiomatic: 〖Duyu〗 Gazetted in the summer of Yongyuan 9.
The exemplar preserves only the stray numerals “1111,” evidently a pagination or scribal artifact.

translations.literal: There is a shrine to the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: A cult site for the Yellow River god stands here.
Rui township lies within the county.

translations.literal: 〖Heyang〗 Summer of the second year of Yongping.
translations.idiomatic: 〖Heyang〗 Established in the summer of Yongping 2.

translations.literal: 〖Xiayang〗 There is Liang Mountain; there is Longmen Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: 〖Xiayang〗 Liang Mountain and Longmen Mountain dominate the relief.

translations.literal: 〖Suyi〗 Summer of the ninth year of Yongyuan.
translations.idiomatic: 〖Suyi〗 Gazetted in the summer of Yongyuan 9.

sentences.zh: ◎ 右扶风秦属内史，武帝分，改名。

translations.literal: ◎ Governor of You Fufeng — under Qin it belonged to the Inner Historian; Emperor Wu split it off and changed the name.
translations.idiomatic: ◎ You Fufeng: territory split from Qin's Inner Historian circuit under Emperor Wu.

sentences.zh: 十五城，户万七千三百五十二，口九万三千九十一。

translations.literal: 〖Huaili〗 In Zhou times called Daqiu; Emperor Gaozu changed it.
translations.idiomatic: 〖Huaili〗 Zhou documents call it Daqiu until Emperor Gaozu rechristened it.
〖Mei〗 Tai pavilion—the ancient Zhou hearth—is noted.

translations.literal: 〖Wugong〗 Summer of the eighth year of Yongping.
translations.idiomatic: 〖Wugong〗 Gazetted in the summer of Yongping 8.

translations.literal: There is Mount Taiyi; originally Zhongnan.
translations.idiomatic: Mount Taiyi preserves the old name Zhongnan.
Chui Mountain—listed in classical glosses as Guowu—stands here.
Xie Valley—the famous Qin-Han pass road—runs here.

translations.literal: 〖Qian〗 There is Wu Yue Mountain; originally named Qian; Qian water rises.
translations.idiomatic: 〖Qian〗 Wu Yue Mountain bore the old name Qian; the Qian River rises here.

translations.literal: There is Hui city; called Huizhong.

translations.idiomatic: 〖Yong〗 Iron works lie within the county.
〖Xunyi〗 Bin township recalls the Bin homeland.

translations.literal: 〖Meiyang〗 There is Qi Mountain; there is Zhou city.
translations.idiomatic: 〖Meiyang〗 Qi Mountain and Zhou city mark Zhou royal geography.

translations.literal: 〖Duyang〗 Summer of the second year of Yonghe.
translations.idiomatic: 〖Duyang〗 Gazetted in the summer of Yonghe 2.

sentences.zh: 右司隶校尉部，郡七，县、邑、侯国百六。

translations.literal: Right: the Inspectorate of the Colonel Director of Retainers — seven commanderies; one hundred six counties, towns, and marquisates in all.
translations.idiomatic: Above concludes the Metropolitan region: seven commanderies and 106 county-level seats under the Colonel of Sili.
